source_text: Ἰδιώμασι δὲ διαφόροις ἕκαστον τῶν ζῴων κέκριται. Εὐσταθὴς μὲν γὰρ ὁ βοῦς, νωθὴς δὲ ὁ ὄνος· θερμὸς δὲ ὁ ἵππος πρὸς ἐπιθυμίαν τοῦ θήλεος· ἀτιθάσσευτος ὁ λύκος, καὶ δολερὸν ἡ ἀλώπηξ· δειλὸν ἡ ἔλαφος· ὁ μύρμηξ φιλόπονος· εὐχάριστον ὁ κύων καὶ πρὸς φιλίαν μνημονικόν. Ὁμοῦ τε γὰρ ἐκτίσθη ἕκαστον, καὶ συνεπηγάγετο ἑαυτῷ τῆς φύσεως τὸ ἰδίωμα. Συναπεγεννήθη ὁ θυμὸς τῷ λέοντι, τὸ μοναστικὸν αὐτοῦ τῆς ζωῆς, τὸ ἀκοινώνητον πρὸς τὸ ὁμόφυλον. Οἷον γάρ τις τύραννος τῶν ἀλόγων, διὰ τὴν ἐκ φύσεως ὑπεροψίαν, τὴν πρὸς τοὺς πολλοὺς ὁμοτιμίαν οὐ καταδέχεται. Ὅς γε οὐδὲ χθιζὴν τροφὴν προσίεται, οὐδ' ἂν τὰ λείψανα τῆς ἑαυτοῦ θήρας ἐπέλθοι· ᾧ καὶ τηλικαῦτα τῆς φωνῆς τὰ ὄργανα ἡ φύσις ἐνέθηκεν, ὥστε πολλὰ τῶν ζῴων ὑπερβάλλοντα τῇ ταχύτητι, μόνῳ πολλάκις ἁλίσκεσθαι τῷ βρυχήματι. Ῥαγδαῖον ἡ πάρδαλις, καὶ ὀξύρροπον ταῖς ὁρμαῖς· ἐπιτήδειον αὐτῇ τὸ σῶμα συνέζευκται τῇ ὑγρότητι καὶ τῷ κούφῳ τοῖς τῆς ψυχῆς κινήμασι συνεπόμενον. Νωθρὰ ἡ φύσις τῆς ἄρκτου, ἰδιότροπον καὶ τὸ ἦθος, ὕπουλον, βαθὺ ἐνδεδυκός. Ὅμοιον ἠμφίεσται καὶ τὸ σῶμα, βαρὺ, συμπεπηγὸς, ἀδιάρθρωτον, πρέπον τῷ ὄντι φωλάδι κατεψυγμένῃ. Ἐὰν ἐπερχώμεθα τῷ λόγῳ πόση τοῖς ἀλόγοις τούτοις ἐνυπάρχει ἀδίδακτος καὶ φυσικὴ τῆς ἑαυτῶν ζωῆς ἐπιμέλεια, ἢ πρὸς τὴν ἡμῶν αὐτῶν φυλακὴν καὶ τῆς τῶν ψυχῶν σωτηρίας πρόνοιαν κινηθησόμεθα, ἢ ἐπιπλέον κατακριθησόμεθα, ὅταν εὑρεθῶμεν καὶ τῆς μιμήσεως τῶν ἀλόγων ἀπολειπόμενοι. Ἄρκτος πολλάκις βαθυτάταις κατατρωθεῖσα πληγαῖς, ἑαυτὴν ἰατρεύει, πάσαις μηχαναῖς τῷ φλόμῳ τούτῳ ξηρὰν τὴν φύσιν ἔχοντι τὰς ὠτειλὰς παραβύουσα. Ἴδοις δ' ἂν καὶ ἀλώπεκα τῷ δακρύῳ τῆς πίτυος ἑαυτὴν ἰωμένην. Χελώνη δὲ σαρκῶν ἐχίδνης ἐμφορηθεῖσα, διὰ τῆς τοῦ ὀριγάνου ἀντιπαθείας φεύγει τὴν βλάβην τοῦ ἰοβόλου. Καὶ ὄφις τὴν ἐν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς βλάβην ἐξιᾶται βοσκηθεὶς μάραθρον. Αἱ δὲ προγνώσεις τῆς περὶ τὸν ἀέρα μεταβολῆς ποίαν οὐχὶ σύνεσιν λογικὴν ἀποκρύπτουσιν; Ὅπου γε τὸ μὲν πρόβατον, χειμῶνος προσιόντος, λάβρως τὴν τροφὴν ἐπεμβάλλεται, ὥσπερ ἐπισιτιζόμενον πρὸς τὴν μέλλουσαν ἔνδειαν. Βόες δὲ κατακεκλεισμένοι χρονίως ἐν ὥρᾳ χειμερινῇ, ἤδη ποτὲ τοῦ ἔαρος προσιόντος, τῇ φυσικῇ αἰσθήσει τὴν μεταβολὴν ἐκδεχόμενοι, ἐκ τῶν βοοστασίων πρὸς τὰς ἐξόδους ὁρῶσι, πάντες ὑφ' ἑνὶ συνθήματι μεταβαλόντες τὸ σχῆμα. Ἤδη δέ τινες τῶν φιλοπόνων καὶ τὸν χερσαῖον ἐχῖνον ἐτήρησαν διπλᾶς ἀναπνοὰς τῇ ἑαυτοῦ καταδύσει μηχανησάμενον, καὶ μέλλοντος μὲν βορέου πνεῖν, ἀποφράσσοντα τὴν ἀρκτῴαν· νότου δὲ πάλιν μεταλαμβάνοντος, εἰς τὴν προσάρκτιον μεταβαίνοντα. Τί διὰ τούτων ἡμῖν ὑποδείκνυται τοῖς ἀνθρώποις; Οὐ μόνον τὸ διὰ πάντων διήκειν τοῦ κτίσαντος ἡμᾶς τὴν ἐπιμέλειαν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ παρὰ τοῖς ἀλόγοις εἰναί τινα τοῦ μέλλοντος αἴσθησιν, ὥστε καὶ ἡμᾶς μὴ τῇ παρούσῃ ζωῇ προστετηκέναι, ἀλλ' ὑπὲρ τοῦ μέλλοντος αἰῶνος τὴν πᾶσαν ἔχειν σπουδήν. Οὐ φιλοπονήσεις περὶ σεαυτοῦ, ἄνθρωπε; οὐκ ἐν τῷ παρόντι αἰῶνι προαποθήσεις τὰς τοῦ μέλλοντος ἀναπαύσεις, πρὸς τὸ ὑπόδειγμα τοῦ μύρμηκος ἀποβλέψας; Ὃς ἐν θέρει τὴν χειμέριον τροφὴν ἑαυτῷ θησαυρίζει, καὶ οὐχ ὅτι μήπω πάρεστι τὰ τοῦ χειμῶνος λυπηρὰ, διὰ ῥᾳθυμίας παραπέμπει τὸν χρόνον· ἀλλὰ σπουδῇ τινι ἀπαραιτήτῳ πρὸς τὴν ἐργασίαν ἑαυτὸν κατατείνει, ἕως ἂν τὴν ἀρκοῦσαν τροφὴν ἐναπόθηται τοῖς ταμιείοις· καὶ οὐδὲ τοῦτο ῥᾳθύμως, ἀλλὰ σοφῇ τινι ἐπινοίᾳ τὴν τροφὴν ἐπιπλεῖστον διαρκεῖν μηχανώμενος.
thought_title: Each animal's natural character and the lessons for humans
orientation: Basil is describing how each kind of animal was created with its own distinctive natural character, and then draws moral lessons from their instinctive care for themselves.
pass_a_gloss: Each of the animals is distinguished by different characteristics. For the ox is steady, and the donkey is sluggish; and the horse is hot toward desire of the female; the wolf is untamable, and the fox is crafty; the deer is timid; the ant is industrious; the dog is grateful and mindful of friendship. For at the same time each was created, and it brought along with itself the characteristic of its nature. The spirit was born together with the lion, its solitary way of life, its refusal to share with its own kind. For like some tyrant of the irrational animals, because of its natural arrogance, it does not accept equal honor with the many. It does not even accept yesterday's food, nor would it even go near the remains of its own hunt; for which also nature has put in such great organs of voice, that many of the animals surpassing it in speed are often caught by the roar alone. The leopard is impetuous, and swift in its impulses; a body suited to it has been yoked together, following the movements of the soul with suppleness and lightness. The nature of the bear is sluggish, and its character is peculiar, deceitful, deeply hidden. It has been clothed with a body similar, heavy, compact, without joints, fitting for a creature that is actually a den-dweller, chilled. If we go through in our account how much untaught and natural care for their own life exists in these irrational animals, either we shall be moved toward our own guarding and toward forethought for the salvation of our souls, or we shall be condemned the more, when we are found falling short even of the imitation of the irrational animals. A bear, often wounded with very deep blows, heals itself, stopping up the scars with all devices with this mullein, which has a dry nature. You could see also a fox healing itself with the resin of the pine. And a tortoise, having gorged itself on the flesh of a viper, through the antipathy of oregano flees the harm of the venomous creature. And a snake heals the harm in its eyes by feeding on fennel. And the forecasts of the change in the air, what rational understanding do they not reveal? Where indeed the sheep, when winter is approaching, greedily takes in food, as if provisioning itself for the coming scarcity. And oxen shut up for a long time in the winter season, when spring is now at last approaching, receiving the change by natural perception, look from the stalls toward the exits, all changing their posture under one signal. And already some of the industrious have observed also the land hedgehog contriving double breathing-holes for its own burrow, and when the north wind is about to blow, blocking up the northern one; and when the south wind in turn takes over, moving to the one facing north. What is shown to us humans through these things? Not only that the care of the one who created us extends through all things, but also that among the irrational animals there is some perception of the future, so that we also should not cling to the present life, but should have all zeal for the age to come. Will you not labor for yourself, O human? Will you not store up in the present age the rests of the future, looking to the example of the ant? Which in summer treasures up for itself the winter food, and not because the hardships of winter are not yet present does it let the time pass in idleness; but with some unrelenting zeal it strains itself toward the work, until it stores away sufficient food in its chambers; and not even this idly, but by some wise contrivance making the food last as long as possible.

choices.why: μοναστικός here means living alone, not monastic in the later institutional sense

choices.english: its not sharing communion with its own kind
choices.why: ἀκοινώνητον is the privative of κοινωνία, 'communion, sharing'; the lion does not share life with its own kind

choices.term: οὐδ' ἂν τὰ λείψανα τῆς ἑαυτοῦ θήρας ἐπέλθοι
choices.english: nor would it even go near the remains of its own hunt
choices.why: ἐπέρχομαι here means 'approach, come upon', not 'attack'; the lion will not even revisit its leftovers
rejected: nor would it attack the remains
nor would it return to the remains

choices.english: fitting for a creature that is actually a den-dweller, chilled
choices.why: τῷ ὄντι is adverbial 'in reality, actually'; κατεψυγμένῃ means 'frozen, chilled', describing the bear's cold den life
rejected: fitting for a truly cold den-dweller
fitting for one who is a den-dweller and frozen

choices.english: what rational understanding do they not reveal
choices.why: The rhetorical question with οὐχί is litotes: 'what understanding do they NOT conceal' = they reveal great understanding

choices.english: moving to the one facing north
choices.why: προσάρκτιος means 'facing the north wind', i.e., the southern opening; the hedgehog moves to the southern vent when the south wind blows

pass_b_english: Each animal is distinguished by its own characteristics. The ox is steady, the donkey sluggish; the horse is hot in its desire for the female; the wolf is untamable, and the fox is cunning; the deer is timid; the ant is industrious; the dog is grateful and remembers friendship. For each was created at the same moment, and it brought along with itself the characteristic of its nature. The lion's anger was born together with it, along with its solitary way of life and its not sharing communion with its own kind. For like some tyrant among the irrational animals, because of its natural arrogance it does not accept equal honor with the many. It does not even accept yesterday's food, nor would it even go near the remains of its own hunt. Nature has placed in it such powerful organs of voice that many animals that surpass it in speed are often caught by the roar alone. The leopard is impetuous and swift in its impulses; its body has been joined to it as suitable, following the movements of its soul with suppleness and lightness. The bear's nature is sluggish, and its character is peculiar, deceitful, deeply hidden. Its body is clothed to match: heavy, compact, without joints, fitting for a creature that is actually a den-dweller, chilled. If we go through in our discussion how much untaught and natural care for their own life exists in these irrational animals, we shall either be moved toward guarding ourselves and providing for the salvation of our souls, or we shall be condemned all the more when we are found falling short even of imitating the irrational animals. A bear, often wounded with the deepest gashes, heals itself, stopping up its wounds by every means with the mullein plant, whose nature is dry. You could also see a fox healing itself with the resin of the pine tree. A tortoise, when it has gorged on viper flesh, escapes the harm of the venom through the antidote of oregano. And a snake heals the damage in its eyes by feeding on fennel. And what rational understanding do the animals' forecasts of changes in the weather not reveal? The sheep, when winter is approaching, takes in its food greedily, as if storing up provisions for the coming scarcity. Cattle that have been shut up for a long time in the winter season, when spring is already approaching, perceive the change by natural sensation and look from their stalls toward the exits, all shifting their posture at a single signal. And already some industrious people have observed that the land hedgehog makes two breathing holes in its burrow, and when the north wind is about to blow, it blocks up the one facing north; but when the south wind takes over again, it moves to the one facing south. What is being shown to us human beings through these things? Not only that the care of our Creator extends through all things, but also that among the irrational animals there is some perception of the future, so that we too should not cling to the present life, but should have all our zeal for the age to come. Will you not labor on your own behalf, O man? Will you not store up beforehand in the present age the rests of the age to come, looking to the example of the ant? It treasures up its winter food in summer, and not because the hardships of winter are not yet here does it let the time pass in idleness; but with an unrelenting eagerness it strains toward the work, until it has stored away sufficient food in its chambers. And it does not do this carelessly, but by some wise contrivance it makes the food last as long as possible.

problems.quote: when the south wind takes over again, it moves to the one facing north
problems.source_quote: νότου δὲ πάλιν μεταλαμβάνοντος, εἰς τὴν προσάρκτιον μεταβαίνοντα
problems.why: προσάρκτιον means 'facing south,' not 'facing north'; the hedgehog moves to the south-facing hole, not north-facing
problems.fix: when the south wind takes over again, it moves to the one facing south
problems.ruling: προσάρκτιον = 'facing south'; νότου = south wind; hedgehog moves to south-facing hole, not north.

edits.old: when the south wind takes over again, it moves to the one facing north
edits.new: when the south wind takes over again, it moves to the one facing south

fixed: Corrected 'facing north' to 'facing south' for προσάρκτιον, which means 'facing south' (πρὸς + ἄρκτος, toward the Bear/North, but the word means facing the north, i.e., south-facing; the hedgehog moves to the south-facing hole when the south wind blows).

problems.quote: moves to the one facing south
problems.why: προσάρκτιος means 'toward the north/northern,' not 'facing south'; the hedgehog moves to the northern vent when south wind blows.
problems.fix: it moves to the one facing north
problems.ruling: προσάρκτιον means 'toward the north'; translating as 'facing south' reverses the meaning.

edits.old: when the south wind takes over again, it moves to the one facing south
edits.new: when the south wind takes over again, it moves to the one facing north

fixed: Corrected 'moves to the one facing south' to 'moves to the one facing north' because προσάρκτιον means 'toward the north' (πρός + ἄρκτος = north), not 'facing south'.

problems.quote: when the south wind takes over again, it moves to the one facing north
problems.source_quote: νότου δὲ πάλιν μεταλαμβάνοντος, εἰς τὴν προσάρκτιον μεταβαίνοντα
problems.why: South wind means move to north-facing hole, not 'facing north' for both; 'προσάρκτιον' means 'facing north', but the first hole blocked is 'τὴν ἀρκτῴαν' (facing north/Arctic), so when south wind comes, it moves to the north-facing hole—this is backwards. When Boreas (north wind) blows, block the north-facing hole; when Notos (south wind) blows, move to the north-facing hole. The English has 'moves to the one facing north' but the context shows this should be the opposite: when south wind comes, it should move to the south-facing hole or the text has an error. Wait: re-reading: ἀρκτῴαν = northern, προσάρκτιον = facing north/northern. This seems contradictory in the Greek itself, but the English repeats 'facing north' for both, which can't be right. Actually 'προσάρκτιον' likely means 'facing the north wind' i.e., south-facing, or there's confusion. The English rendering as 'facing north' for both makes no functional sense; the hedgehog would suffocate. The Greek likely means opposite holes.
problems.fix: when the south wind takes over again, it moves to the one facing south

edits.old: when the south wind takes over again, it moves to the one facing north
edits.new: when the south wind takes over again, it moves to the one facing south

fixed: The English repeats 'facing north' for both holes, which makes no functional sense; the Greek 'προσάρκτιον' in context means the hole facing away from the north wind, i.e., facing south, so the hedgehog moves to the south-facing hole when the south wind blows.

last_rejected.quote: It does not even accept yesterday's food
last_rejected.source_quote: Ὅς γε οὐδὲ χθιζὴν τροφὴν προσίεται
last_rejected.why: χθιζὴν means 'yesterday's' but the sense is 'it does not even accept food from yesterday (leftover/prey from before)'; 'accept' for προσίεται is odd here—better 'take' or 'receive'
last_rejected.fix: It does not even take food from yesterday
last_rejected.ruling: 'yesterday's food' accurately renders χθιζὴν τροφήν; 'accept' is within normal range for προσίεται.

last_rejected.quote: the mullein plant, whose nature is dry
last_rejected.source_quote: τῷ φλόμῳ τούτῳ ξηρὰν τὴν φύσιν ἔχοντι
last_rejected.why: Greek says mullein 'having dry nature,' not 'whose nature is dry'—the plant itself is dry, not that it possesses a quality called 'dry nature.'
last_rejected.fix: the mullein, which is dry by nature
last_rejected.ruling: ξηρὰν τὴν φύσιν ἔχοντι = 'having dry nature'; 'whose nature is dry' is equivalent, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: the resin of the pine tree
last_rejected.why: δάκρυον means 'tear' or 'sap/tear of resin,' but 'resin' alone loses the specific wordplay; 'pine-tears' or 'pine resin' would be closer.
last_rejected.ruling: δάκρυον of πίτυς denotes pine resin/sap; 'resin' is within normal range, no meaning lost.

last_rejected.why: κατεψυγμένῃ is passive/perfect participle 'chilled through' or 'frozen,' describing the bear's state, not an appositive 'a den-dweller, chilled.'
last_rejected.fix: a den-dweller that is chilled through
last_rejected.ruling: φωλάδι κατεψυγμένῃ is dative agreeing with φωλάδι; 'den-dweller, chilled' captures sense adequately.

last_rejected.quote: rests of the age to come
last_rejected.why: ἀνάπαυσις means 'rest' singular or plural 'times of rest/relief'; 'rests' is awkward and potentially misleading as countable repose-periods rather than 'rest' or 'relief.'
last_rejected.fix: the rest of the age to come
last_rejected.ruling: ἀναπαύσεις plural 'rests' is awkward but within meaning range; no reader misled about future-age rest.
